name: The Hershey Company
moat_justification: Strong but not wide-open moat: dominant US chocolate position (~36% share of the US chocolate aisle vs Mars ~29%, per Morningstar), flagship brands (Reese's, Hershey's, Kisses) with proven pricing power — FY2026 revenue growth is being carried by price while volumes fall — entrenched retail relationships and scale cost advantages, and high through-cycle returns on capital. Held to 7, not 8-9, because pricing is now visibly costing volume (Q2 2026 total volume ~-8%, North America Confectionery ~-10%), cocoa is structurally more expensive, and GLP-1 / health trends are a slow demand erosion force with no network-effect or switching-cost protection.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: High-quality wide-brand moat (7/10) but slow-growing and priced for perfection — weighted IRR 9.8% at $164.28 vs weighted IV@15% $92.59; only clears Andrew's 15% hurdle below ~$93.
moat_for: ~36% US chocolate share, #1 position ahead of Mars
Flagship brands (Reese's, Hershey's, Kisses) with proven pricing power
Entrenched retail shelf relationships; critical partner for retailers
Scale cost advantage and high through-cycle returns on capital
moat_against: Pricing now costing volume: Q2 2026 volume ~-8%, NA Confectionery ~-10%
Structurally elevated cocoa costs; hedge book not positioned to capture relief in 2026
GLP-1 appetite suppression and health/sugar trends erode category demand slowly
Mars and Mondelez competition; private label at the value end
Salty-snacks supply/execution issues (Dot's multipacks, logistics costs)
